newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, rollovers active.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, rollovers active.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended on a weak note on Wednesday on a dearth of buying incentives and dealers said a test of the 18,000 points psychological support level might be on the cards in the near term.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 295 points to close at 18,285 after hitting a low of 18,205.
"It wouldn't surprise me to see it bounce below 18,000 on an intra-day basis but a close below that level would mean further weakness," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
He said the market was likely to be somewhat underpinned ahead of the Japanese financial year end on March 31.
"At the back of our minds is the fact that the Japanese will be closing their books at the end of the month, so that should be mildly supportive," he said.
Dealers said rollover activity was becoming increasingly active ahead of the March contract's expiry next week.
"Most of the rollover activity has been selling of the June contract, indicating that most people would prefer to be short," said the trader.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 336.7 against its opening 335.0 on volume of 726 lots.
